gcx_context: <your gcx context, or delete this line to use the current one>
stack_notes: <optional: anything a colleague would tell a new joiner, e.g. which Prometheus datasource to use. Both configurations see it.>
answer_key_written: <date, and where the answers came from: your own knowledge, code, config or raw traces. Never from the agent or the graph.>

questions.question: What does <service> in <cluster / environment> connect to over the network? Include databases, caches and where it sends its own telemetry, and include connections that do not appear in its traces.
If the database behind <service> in <cluster / environment> went down, which services would be affected, directly or transitively, up to the entry points that receive its traffic?
must_include: <the entry point, e.g. an ingress or user-facing app>
must_not_include: <a service that shares callers but not the database>

questions.question: Which <namespace / cluster> does <service> run in, in our <region described in words, not its label> production cluster?

questions._note: Optional and advanced. Use a past incident with a written root cause (a post-incident review), pin the window to the incident, and take the answer from the review, never from the agent or the graph. Run it 5 times per configuration: it varies more than the other questions.
questions.question: An alert fired at <time> UTC on <date>: <alert name> for <service> in <cluster / environment>. What caused it? Find where the problem started and how it led to the alert.
questions.answer_format: End your answer with the root cause on the first line, then each step from it to the alert, one per line, between a line that says ANSWER and a line that says END.
must_include: <the mechanism that connected it to the symptom>
must_not_include: <the alerting service, if the cause was elsewhere>

questions.question: How many <service> replicas were available in <cluster / environment> at the end of the time window?
Which services call <service> in <cluster / environment>?
must_not_include: <something it calls, rather than something that calls it>

questions.question: What does <service> in <cluster / environment> depend on? List the services, databases and caches it calls.
If <database or cache> in <cluster / environment> went down, which services would be affected, directly or through one other service?
<service> runs in several places. Which <namespace / region / cluster> is the one in <environment>?
Which Kubernetes nodes (or cloud resources) were running <service> in <cluster / environment> at the end of the time window?
Which of the services, databases and caches that <service> calls in <cluster / environment> returned failed calls during the time window?

_note: Five core questions run by default: hidden dependencies, deep blast radius, finding the right system without its label, an incident root cause and a control. The rest are optional extras ("optional": true); run them with --all. Delete I1 if you don't have a past incident with a written root cause.
